plan.question: Why did compiling the airbench96-style port's forward+backward with torch.compile (mode='max-autotune-no-cudagraphs', PyTorch 2.4) plus a foreach/fused SGD make the timed prepare+train run slower (12.07 s vs 9.43 s at 9 epochs) instead of faster, with accuracy unchanged? Specifically: is the extra ~2.6 s a fixed cost leaking into the timed region (Dynamo guard failures or recompiles when train/eval mode, requires_grad, BN buffers or new shapes change after build; autotuning or cuDNN benchmark redone on the first real step; lazy compilation of the backward), or a real per-step slowdown of Inductor-generated conv/BN/GELU kernels compared with eager cuDNN for small-resolution, channels_last fp16 CNNs? Which diagnostics (per-epoch timing, TORCH_LOGS recompiles, Dynamo cache stats) and which fixes (compiling only non-conv parts, mode='default', static shapes, dropping the ragged batch, CUDA graphs) recover the expected 10–20% speedup?

rubric: Measures torch.compile/Inductor (or a comparable DL compiler such as XLA or TVM) for CNN training against eager cuDNN, with per-step timing reported separately from compile or warm-up time
Names concrete causes of compiled-mode slowdowns or recompiles, e.g. guard failures, dynamic shapes, train/eval mode switches, autotuning, or conv lowering choices, and gives a fix or diagnostic
Covers short, overhead-dominated runs (small images, ~seconds per epoch, single GPU, few CPU cores) where fixed costs make up a meaningful share of wall time
Gives actionable settings (compile mode, which ops to compile, CUDA graphs, static shapes, warm-up strategy) that can be used with PyTorch 2.4 and no new packages
exclude: Methods relying on pretrained weights, external data, or transfer learning
Test-time augmentation or anything using the test set during training
Approaches needing package installs or PyTorch versions other than 2.4 (e.g., newer compile features only in 2.5+)
Large-scale distributed/multi-GPU or LLM-only compiler studies with no CNN relevance
Inference-only compilation papers with no training-step measurements
